messages:
maria: Heads up — seeing noisy ECC/Xid spikes on gpu-node-12 (us-west) over the last 8m. Nodes flapping between healthy->degraded. Proposing we discuss a cordon+backoff policy that avoids churn but protects SLAs. Logs attached in thread.
infra-bot: [alert] gpu-health: gpu-node-12 ECC spike count=7 window=10m, Xid errors=4. mark=warning :rotating_light:
jon: +1 on avoiding churn. Idea: soft-cordon (no new pods) after 2 probe failures in 5m, run memtest/kminer probe, then escalate to drain only after sustained failures (eg 3 probes over 30m). Keeps short lived blips from causing evictions.
lee: we should keep hysteresis. proposed knobs:
- probe_failure_threshold=2
- probe_window=5m
- escalate_threshold=3
- escalate_window=30m
- soft_cordon_ttl=15m (auto-uncordon if health clears)
Also track consecutive_soft_cordons before hard drain.
sasha: slurm note: when we cordon nodes backing a Slurm partition, we must respect requeue vs cancel. For Dedicated/Slurm nodes, prefer maintenance mode + drain after drain-window to avoid job kill storms. Slurm controller should be told to requeue low-priority tasks only.
taylor: cost angle: frequent hard drains = more preemptions and instance replacements, which spikes spot spend and reduces throughput. In tight regions (us-west) tighten escalate_window to avoid losing capacity; in spare regions allow faster drains. region-aware thresholds pls.
devops: draft rollout plan:
1) implement soft-cordon + probe binary in health-agent (v0.12)
2) add metrics: gpu_probe_failures, soft_cordon_count, hard_drain_count, unavail_gpu_minutes
3) canary in staging -> canary US-EAST pool (5 nodes) -> grad rollout to non-prod -> prod phased by region
4) automated memtest job: infra-bot triggers self-test when soft-cordon enters >1
kubectl snippet for k8s path:
```bash
# soft cordon (no evict)
kubectl label node gpu-node-12 cordon=soft --overwrite
# soft drain: cordon + allow-pods-with-annotation=soft-evict
kubectl drain gpu-node-12 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=600 --pod-selector=\"evictable!=false\"
# hard drain (forceful)
kubectl drain gpu-node-12 --force --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=120
```
maria: good. How do we validate the policy itself? Need a synthetic-failure harness and postmortem criteria (SLO impact, cost delta).
jon: test harness ideas:
- Inject ECC spike via telemetry simulator to one GPU and assert soft_cordon is applied and memtest runs.
- Simulate sustained Xid to trigger escalate path and verify Slurm requeue behavior and k8s eviction ordering.
- Run chaos window with load generator and ensure 95th latency and QPS unaffected beyond 5%.
Also add alerts for \"cordon_revert_failure\" (auto-uncordon failing).
lee: backoff algo suggestion:
- backoff steps = [15m, 1h, 4h]
- each soft-cordon increments step if failures reoccur within step window
- reset counter after 12h clear
This limits repeated short-lived interventions but still isolates genuinely flaky hardware.
sasha: here's a short runbook snippet for on-call:
\"If node enters soft-cordon: 1) check gpu_health_traces 2) trigger memtest via infra-bot 3) if memtest passes -> uncordon; if fails -> mark escalate and notify hw-replacement queue. For Slurm-backed nodes, inform scheduler-admins before hard drain.\"
(internal doc) https://redwood.internal/runbooks/gpu-cordon-backoff
infra-bot: scheduled: memtest job queued for gpu-node-12 -> job-id=mt-2026-03-01-99. Will post results to thread when done.
taylor: add dashboard panels: drain_surge_rate (1h), preempt_cost_delta (24h), region_capacity_headroom. alert: >5 hard drains in 1h => page infra@ oncall.
maria: OK actionable list:
- devops: implement soft-cordon + memtest trigger (owner: @devops)
- eng-infra: add metrics and backoff state to health-agent (owner: @lee & @jon)
- sasha: update Slurm requeue policy and add runbook step
- taylor: add cost panels and alert rules
I'll create a PR for the policy doc and canary checklist. thanks everyone :thumbsup:
